headline: The AI-chip unwind spreads from Wall Street to Asia's chip markets, with Dell's beat the one counterpoint before today's 14:30 US data

findings.headline: Asia's chipmakers take the hit from Nvidia's reversal
findings.body: Doubts about whether AI data-centre spending will pay back returned after Nvidia fell 5.9% on Tuesday, and Asia's chip-heavy markets took the brunt overnight: Samsung and SK hynix fell around 9% in Seoul, TSMC about 8% and MediaTek about 10% in Taipei. Because single chip names carry so much index weight in Taiwan and Korea, a company story becomes a market story there, while Hong Kong is insulated by domestic policy. The Bank of Korea decides on Thursday, a further risk for the most stretched of these markets.

Al Jazeera: Asia's stock markets dive as doubts swirl over AI boom

findings.headline: Dell's record quarter argues the other side of the AI-capex debate
findings.body: After the close Dell reported record quarterly revenue of $54.9 billion, up 103% on the year on AI-server demand, lifted its full-year revenue guide to $202 billion from $192 billion and added a $25 billion buyback; the shares rose about 4-5% after hours having fallen sharply into the print. That is hard evidence of AI orders converting into revenue, the opposite of the payback worry that hit Nvidia. Whether chips stabilise at the US open will show which reading the market leans to.

findings.headline: Hot Australian inflation sets the tone for the 14:30 US data block
findings.body: Australia's October CPI rose 4.9% year on year, up from 4.3%, driven by electricity after rebates ended and by fuel; trimmed-mean was 3.8%. It adds to a global inflation backdrop just as US Q3 GDP, October PCE, durable goods and jobless claims all land at 14:30 Zurich, with a December Fed hike already largely priced. A hot core PCE is the bigger risk, because it would open the door to more than one hike while chips and miners are already lagging.

sources.label: ABS: CPI rose 4.9% in the year to October 2026

view: Our view: This is still rotation inside risk, out of AI chips and metals and into defensives and value, rather than a broad flight to safety, and Dell's numbers give the chip bulls something concrete to lean on. Today's core PCE decides whether the rotation turns into wider de-risking into the thin Thanksgiving session.
